# GEO report: trailhead **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. All results are read from code. I ran no live check. ## Code score: 46–54/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 21 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 10.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 46. High = (10.5 + 2) ÷ 23 × 100 = 54. Four rules have problems: the app renders only in the browser, the sitemap link in robots.txt is relative, every page shares one title and description, and the guides page is hidden from search. The only unknown is the canonical address, because the site's real domain isn't declared. The band comes from the low number. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Turn on server rendering - **Why it matters:** With `ssr: false`, crawlers get an empty page shell and must run JavaScript to see any text. - **Where:** `nuxt.config.ts:2` - **What the code says:** `ssr: false,` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 59–67 ### 2. Make the robots.txt Sitemap line an absolute URL - **Why it matters:** The sitemap spec requires a full URL. A relative path may be ignored, so crawlers may not find your sitemap. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4` - **What the code says:** `Sitemap: /sitemap.xml` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 54–63 ### 3. Link to the guides page with a real link - **Why it matters:** The home page reaches `/guides` only through a button click handler. Crawlers follow `` links, not script actions. - **Where:** `pages/index.vue:8` - **What the code says:** `` - **Size:** Small (use ``) - **Score after this:** 54–63. Items 2 and 3 each add the same 2 points. Applied alone on top of the current score, each gives that range. ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is reachable and parseable | Clear | `public/robots.txt`; plain text and tiny. The relative Sitemap line is scored under GEO-011. | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers can get in | Clear | `public/robots.txt:2` blocks only `/admin`. I assumed you want to be found. | | GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | `/` is fine, but `/guides` gets `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` in `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` (1 of 2 routes clear). | | GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on your own domain | Can't tell | No canonical is set anywhere. No domain is declared; `trailhead.example` in the sitemap looks like a placeholder. | | GEO-003 | Main content is in the server HTML | Problem | `nuxt.config.ts:2` `ssr: false`, site-wide. | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD found. | | GEO-011 | Valid, discoverable sitemap | Problem | `public/robots.txt:4` is relative. `public/sitemap.xml` itself is valid. | | GEO-012 | Title, description and lang | Problem | `app.vue:2` and `nuxt.config.ts:6` give every page the same title and description. `lang="en"` is set. | | GEO-016 | Key pages reachable by real links | Problem | `pages/index.vue:8`; `/guides` has no `` link (0 of 1 clear). | | GEO-017 | No snippet restrictions | Clear | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0` found in the head tags, `nuxt.config.ts` or `server/middleware/headers.ts`. | | GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | I read `pages/*.vue`. They have no images, and the button has text. | | GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | No mobile app declared. | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not applicable | None present; never scored. | | GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not applicable | Not an app; never scored. | ## Other problems found - **Sitemap lists a noindex page:** `public/sitemap.xml:4` has `https://trailhead.example/guides`, but `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` has `setResponseHeader(event, 'X-Robots-Tag', 'noindex');` for `/guides`. Remove the header, or drop the URL from the sitemap. If the guides are meant to be found, remove the header. - **Placeholder domain:** `public/sitemap.xml:3` has `https://trailhead.example/`. Replace it with the real origin. ## Worth considering - **Give each page its own title and description:** `pages/guides.vue:4`: `

Routes graded from easy to strenuous.

`. Add `useHead` with a title such as "Trail guides – Trailhead", and a description that matches the page. - **Set the site URL in Nuxt config:** `nuxt.config.ts:1` has no `site.url`. Declare the real origin so canonicals and sitemap URLs can be built from it. - **Add a canonical link per page:** `app.vue:2` sets only a title. Once the origin is known, add an absolute `rel="canonical"` for each page. - **Fill out the thin pages:** `pages/guides.vue:4` promises "Routes graded from easy to strenuous", but no routes are listed. Add the actual guides as text, ideally one page per route with its own URL. - **Say what the home page offers:** `pages/index.vue:7`: `

Walks across the Peak District

`. The page has only a heading and a button. Add a short intro and links to featured walks. - **Label the site with structured data:** Add `WebSite` or `Organization` JSON-LD with the name and URL the site already shows. - **Add `` to the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:3-4` has no dates. Add them if you have real update dates. - **Generate the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml` is hand-kept. A Nuxt sitemap module could build it from your routes. - **Remove the redundant `/admin` noindex:** `pages/admin.vue:2` and `public/robots.txt:2` both cover it. This looks deliberate, so leave it as is. Note that a robots.txt block stops crawlers from ever seeing the page's noindex tag. That doesn't matter if the goal is simply to keep the page out of crawls. ## Can't tell from code - **GEO-015 (canonical):** the real domain isn't declared. Tell me the domain and add canonicals to settle this. - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs ` to check real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Headers set outside the repo:** hosting or CDN rules could add more `X-Robots-Tag` values (GEO-014, GEO-017). ## Assumptions - You want search engines and AI tools to find this site, including the guides page. - `/admin` is meant to stay private, so I left it out of the sampled routes. I sampled `/` and `/guides`, which is every public route. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
